title: Introduce conditional PrefixList egress policy, cross-account DNS relay, and rollback hooks for controlplane
author: Diego Alvarez
release_notes: Add conditional egress via AWS PrefixLists, enable cross-account Route53 Resolver relay for private control planes, and introduce deterministic rollback hooks for peerings/endpoints. No API changes. Backwards-compatible installer flags added.
body:
Motivation: Private control planes need tighter, auditable egress controls and a safe automated rollback path during upgrades. This PR introduces a conditional egress policy driven by AWS PrefixLists (so customers can maintain CIDR sets centrally), a small cross-account DNS relay construct using Route53 Resolver rules + outbound endpoints, and explicit rollback hooks that the installer can invoke to tear down partially-applied peering/endpoints without leaving dangling state.

What changed (high level):
- terraform/modules/network: new prefixlist_egress module (conditionals for managed vs customer-supplied prefix-lists) and hooks for associating with NAT/GW/ENI-level rules.
- terraform/modules/dns: added resolver-relay module that creates ResolverRules, Inbound/Outbound endpoints, and IAM role policy templates for cross-account rule association.
- installer/orchestrator: introduce StepRunner rollback hook interface and a new step type "conditional-egress" that validates prefixlist attachments pre-apply and records rollback transactions in state.
- helm/redwood-private: minor values.yaml additions to enable egress enforcement and DNS relay config toggles.
- docs/installer: new operational guide for configuring PrefixLists, granting cross-account resolver permissions, and performing a safe rollback.

Design notes:
- The PrefixList module supports two modes: managed (installer creates/updates a PrefixList and exports the ID) or referenced (customer supplies an existing PrefixList ID). Attachments to NATs/route tables are gated by subnet tags (controlplane: true) to avoid accidental network-wide changes.
- DNS relay uses Route53 Resolver inbound endpoints in the control plane account and outbound endpoints in tenant account(s) with ResolverRule associations created cross-account. We add a reconciliation loop in the installer to assert rule health.
- Rollback hooks are recorded as idempotent Terraform null_resources with local-exec scriptlets (kept minimal) that the StepRunner can call to reverse peering attachments, delete resolver rule associations, and detach prefixlist references. Hooks are also surfaced in the console as a rollback preview before executing.

Checklist (tested):
- [x] Terraform plan/apply in CI for both managed and referenced prefixlist modes
- [x] End-to-end controlplane deploy to a staging account (peering + resolver rules validated)
- [x] Simulated partial failure during peering creation and successful rollback via StepRunner
- [x] Helm values toggles tested with smoke deploy of private controlplane chart
- [x] Security review for IAM policies granting only Resolver associations and PrefixList describe/modify where necessary

Upgrade/rollout plan:
1) Roll out installer bits (no infra changes yet) to allow operator to opt-in via values.
2) Create PrefixList in a single region and run an opt-in apply to attach to controlplane subnets (can be reverted).
3) Enable resolver relay and validate cross-account DNS resolution using ephemeral test records.
4) Promote to production using canary deployment across two regions, using the rollback hook if any validation fails.

Rollback semantics:
- Hooks are idempotent: running rollback twice has no additional effect.
- Rollback will: remove resolver rule associations, delete cross-account route53 associations only if they were created by the installer, detach and remove PrefixList associations (for managed mode), and remove transient peering attachments while leaving long-lived VPCs intact.

Security considerations:
- All cross-account actions require explicit Linear approvals and customer to provide a Resolver association IAM role or opt into installer-created short-lived role.
- The installer will not overwrite existing customer-managed ResolverRules unless the operator runs with --force.

Operational notes for SRE:
- New metrics exported in console: prefixlist.attach_count, resolver.rule_sync_status, rollback.exec_duration. Alerts recommended for resolver.rule_sync_status != 0 for >5m.
- CLI: added 'redwood-installer rollback --step <name>' to replay recorded rollback hooks for a specific step.

Related work: ENG-1023 (subnet ownership tagging), PR #71288 (subnet reconciliation), and the resolver work in INF-387.

Please see changed_files for per-path notes and the commit list below.

review_comments: Priya Nandakumar: Please confirm the default IAM policy does not allow broad ec2:ModifyPrefixList entries across accounts. Also request a short rationale for using PrefixLists vs security-groups for egress control.
